Subject: SOC 2 exception follow-up: evidence & bridge letter request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Brightline's engagement team flagged the control exception in the change-management control family that occurred during the 2026 Type II period (control ID CM-4). Our auditors have requested: 1) the status of remediation for CM-4, 2) any interim compensating controls you had in place after the finding, and 3) whether Redwood can provide a short management statement (bridge letter) clarifying the exception window and remediation commitment for our FY26 audit file.

Specifically, Jordan asked for a management response memo plus any evidence you can share by Feb 15 so they can wrap up their fieldwork. I realize some material is sensitive — if a redacted bundle or a signed bridge letter works, that would be fine.

Can you confirm who owns the remediation and whether you can provide a draft bridge letter and timeline for closure?

Best,
Emily Hansen
Senior Risk Manager
Pacifica Bank

--

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and for flagging the auditor's timeline. We're treating CM-4 as high priority.

Quick answers up front:
- Remediation owner: Rishi (copied) will own the technical root-cause and confirm evidence.
- Interim compensating controls: we had an elevated code-review and deployment gating process in place from 2026-11-01 through 2026-12-15; I can summarize those steps in the management memo.
- Bridge letter: yes, we can provide a short signed bridge letter that describes the exception window and confirms the remediation plan and target dates.

Rishi — can you share the management response draft and the evidence list by EOD tomorrow? Marissa — please prepare a short note we can include describing customer-impact assessment and monitoring. Emily/Jordan — would a Feb 16 signed bridge letter meet the auditor deadline or do you need it sooner?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

Subject: Draft: management response & remediation plan for CM-4

Kimberly / team / Emily / Jordan —

Attached is the draft management response (management_response_draft.pdf) and the remediation plan spreadsheet (remediation_plan_v2.xlsx). Highlights:

1) Root cause: An automated deployment approval rule was mistakenly excluded from the staging-to-prod pipeline during a config migration in late Oct 2026, which allowed one change to bypass the normal peer-review gating (CM-4 trigger).

2) Remediation steps completed: re-enabled approval rule (2026-11-03), retroactive code-review of the single deployment (evidence: review_comments_20261104.zip), and a one-week recall where we froze risky change merges (2026-11-04 — 2026-11-10).

3) Remaining actions: formalize pipeline validation checks in CI (owner: Infra Eng — ETA 2027-03-01), add automated alerting to detect approval-rule disables (owner: SRE — ETA 2027-02-28), and update change-management runbook (owner: Ops — ETA 2027-02-20).

4) Compensating controls while remediating: increased manual approvals, daily deployment scoreboard review, and targeted monitoring of risky services (documented in remediation_plan_v2.xlsx).

5) Evidence bundle proposed for auditors: evidence_summary.zip (contains logs, review artifacts, and change tickets). We will redact any customer-identifiable logs.

If this looks good I can convert the PDF into a signed management statement and draft a bridge letter for Jordan/Emily to review.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Applied Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: management_response_draft.pdf, remediation_plan_v2.xlsx, evidence_summary.zip

Thanks Rishi — that is helpful and concise. A couple of follow-ups from Jordan:

1) For the bridge letter the auditor wants an explicit statement of the exception window (start/end dates) and whether any additional exceptions were discovered after the window closed. Can you confirm the exact dates we should state for CM-4?
2) Jordan also asked for a one-paragraph description of the interim compensating control that was in place for the audit team file (they prefer a crisp sentence they can insert into the audit report).

If you can give the precise dates and the one-paragraph compensating-control sentence today, we'll be able to include your statement in the audit file. Feb 15 is still the target for final signed items.

Appreciate the speed here.

Emily
